opportunities.name: Developer-tool lead research (HN + GitHub → note)
opportunities.description: For a given open-source project, find its top Hacker News story and its GitHub repo stats, then log a 'Lead' note with HN title/points/age and GitHub stars/last release date.
steps: Open Hacker News search (Algolia) and select the search box (ctrl+a to clear)
Type {project} and press Enter; read the top story's title, points and age
Open GitHub, click 'Search or jump to', type {project} and press Enter
Click the matching repository in the results (e.g. owner/{project})
Read star count and latest release date from the repo sidebar
Open the Notes app, click 'New note'
Type 'Lead: {project}. HN "{top story title}" ({points} pts, {age}); GitHub {stars} stars, last release {release date}' and press Enter

instances.values: project=Bun (HN 'Anthropic acquires Bun' 2192 pts; oven-sh/bun 96.2k stars); interrupted by CourtListener activity
project=deno (GitHub search only; no HN search or note, left unfinished)

opportunities.name: Country fact-check (World Bank indicator + BBC context → note)
opportunities.description: For a given country, look up World Bank development indicators (e.g. life expectancy), find a related recent BBC article, and log a 'Fact-check' note combining the two.
steps: Open World Bank Open Data and click the 'Search data e.g. GDP, population, Indonesia' box
Type {country} (using the World Bank spelling, e.g. 'Viet Nam'), then press Enter or pick the country suggestion
Read the needed indicator (e.g. life expectancy at birth) on the country page
Open BBC, accept cookies if asked, click 'Open menu' and then 'Search news, topics and more'
Type '{country} {topic}' and press Enter; open the most relevant recent article
Open Notes, click 'New note', type 'Fact-check {country}: {indicator} {value} ({year}). Context: {article headline} ({age})' and press Enter

instances.values: country=Kenya, topic=health; life expectancy 64 (2024); Ebola article
country=Vietnam/Viet Nam, topic=climate; Kenya vs Viet Nam comparison; coffee/climate article; no note was saved
country=Argentina (only the World Bank search; search kept showing stale suggestions, left unfinished)

opportunities.name: Company legal-story pitch (CourtListener + Wikipedia → email)
opportunities.description: For a given company, search CourtListener for a court case, look up company facts on Wikipedia, and draft a pitch email to an editor.
steps: Open CourtListener and click the 'Keyword(s) search with operators' box (ctrl+a to clear)
Type {company} and press Enter; open a relevant opinion and note its name, court and filing date
Open Wikipedia, type {company} into 'Search Wikipedia' and press Enter (pick the company article if a disambiguation page appears)
Note the HQ and CEO
Open the mail app, compose a new message: To={editor email}, Subject='Pitch: {company} in court'
Body: 'Hi {editor}, {case name} ({court}, filed {date}). {company}: HQ {hq}, CEO {ceo}. Worth a piece?'
Send or discard

instances.values: company=Uber; case Uber v. Uber (Ohio Ct. App. 2017); email to lena@example.com (draft discarded)
company=Airbnb (only the CourtListener search; resubmitted several times)
company=Tesla (CourtListener search did not refresh the results; Wikipedia Tesla → Tesla, Inc.; no email)
